abstract: The results of a 7-year monitoring of 230 patients with non-seminomatous testicular tumors are reported with respect to the employment of radioimmunoanalysis of alpha-fetoprotein and beta-human chorionic gonadotropin levels and CT examinations of retroperitoneum and lungs. Prior to orchiectomy, elevated levels of at least one of these markers were found in 79% of patients. After orchiectomy, tumor marker levels were in 70.4% of patients in agreement with the results of CT examinations. After the completion of chemotherapy, in more than a half of patients normal tumor marker levels and positive CT findings were observed. These results were most often due to the presence of mature teratoma. In Stage I patients the advantages of tumor marker determinations and CT examinations in the early detection of tumor progression have fully been confirmed.
abstract_ja: 非セミノーマ性精巣胚細胞腫瘍の患者230例を7年間にわたり経過観察した結果を報告する。αフェトプロテイン(AFP)およびβ-ヒト絨毛性ゴナドトロピン(β-hCG)の放射免疫測定法と、後腹膜および肺のコンピュータ断層撮影(CT)検査を用いた。精巣摘除術前に、患者の79%で少なくとも1つのマーカーの上昇がみられた。精巣摘除術後は、70.4%の患者で腫瘍マーカー値がCT所見と一致していた。化学療法の完了後、半数以上の患者で正常な腫瘍マーカー値とCT陽性所見が観察された。これらの結果はほとんどの場合、成熟奇形腫の存在によるものであった。病期Iの患者では、腫瘍マーカー測定とCT検査が病勢進行の早期発見に有用であることが改めて確認された。
